warnings: AREA IS NOT A LAYOUT NUMBER. Table IV's 'Area (F^2)' is literally transistor count x 9 F^2 (2T1SOT = 9*2, 3T2SOT = 9*3). 9 F^2 for a W = 3F device leaves no room for source/drain contacts, spacing or the MTJ/HM stack footprint; a realistic 3F-wide MRAM access device is 12-16 F^2. The 27 F^2 for 3T2SOT is therefore an optimistic lower bound.

The same table assigns 40.33 F^2 to the SINGLE 1T1MTJ STT access transistor - a 4.5x area ratio against the 9 F^2 SOT transistor for only a ~2x drive-current ratio (75 uA vs 33 uA). The cell stores 1 bit in 2 MTJs and 3 transistors. If you model it in DESTINY as an ordinary 1-MTJ cell you will halve the storage-element count and get the wrong array energy. There is no DESTINY key for a differential 2-MTJ cell.
Write is UNIDIRECTIONAL and requires a read-before-write. Set and Reset currents/energies are identical by construction, which is unusual and worth a comment in the .cell file.
Temperature is never stated. 45 nm PTM default (typically 300 K / 27 C) is the reasonable assumption but the paper does not say so.
Abstract says 'the write latency of the proposed design can be reduced to 0.3 ns' while Table IV says 0.26 ns. Use 0.26 ns (the table).

unmapped_parameters: Table I also lists for SRAM: Resistance On = 1000 ohm, Resistance Off = 1000000 ohm, Reset Current = 600 uA, Reset Pulse = 50 ns, Set Current = 75 uA, Set Pulse = 400 ns. These are NOT SRAM parameters - see warnings.
warnings: THE SRAM COLUMN OF TABLE I IS NOT A VALID SRAM CELL SPECIFICATION. 'Resistance On = 1000 ohm / Resistance Off = 1000000 ohm', 'Reset Pulse = 50 ns' and 'Set Pulse = 400 ns' are meaningless for a 16 nm 6T SRAM (which writes in tens of picoseconds). These rows look like leftovers from an unedited NVSim resistive-memory cell template - most plausibly a PCRAM/memristor template, given 1 kOhm / 1 MOhm and 50 ns / 400 ns. DO NOT PORT THIS COLUMN. Build the SRAM baseline from DESTINY's own 16 nm SRAM cell instead.

Because the SRAM baseline is mis-specified, every SRAM-relative ratio in Figs. 4-7 (the paper's entire results section) rests on a questionable reference point. Treat the 66.45% leakage / 56% energy / 28% speed headline claims as unvalidated.
No SRAMCellNMOSWidth / SRAMCellPMOSWidth, no read voltage, no read pulse, no min sense voltage.

device_geometry: 1T1MTJ. Table 1 gives cell area 10 F^2 at aspect ratio 1.0 with a 6 F access transistor. Note the same tension as DESTINY's shipped cell: a 6 F wide device does not fit inside 10 F^2, so treat the area as the MTJ stack footprint rather than the full bit-cell. The paper's own Tables 3-4 sweep area over 10-30 F^2 and aspect ratio over 0.3-2.0, which is the study this project mirrors for SOT.
